why: RC-02. The criterion-content oracle compares predicate-registry.json to tools/phase_content.py and fails on any difference -- which makes a HAND edit of a criterion a failing build, and makes a DERIVATION edit invisible. The recheck measured it: one hunk replacing the ('SalesAgreement','performed') spec, then `python3 tools/author_phase_content.py`, and the whole G2-01 defect is back at exit 0, 268,829 checks, with all 27 negative fixtures still rejecting. A checker that compares an artifact to a source the same author controls is not a checker. Every assertion below is written BY HAND against the live registry and is never generated from anything: author_phase_content.py does not read this file and cannot write it, so regenerating the registry from a weakened derivation now fails HERE, naming the conjunct that went missing. RC2-02, the same argument one operator over and found the same way -- by mutation, not by reading: these rows asserted CONTAINMENT, and a conjunct kept verbatim inside an `any` beside a trivially-true alternative is contained by the body while being demanded by nothing. Every `why` below is written as a demand, so each row now says which it means: `disjoined` defaults to false and the four rows whose requirement really is conditional name their branch.

how_to_read.pin: one predicate id, the findings and decisions that put each requirement there, and the `require` rows that must hold of its body in the committed predicate-registry.json
how_to_read.matching: a row matches when SOME node of the body carries that `op` and satisfies every constraint on the row. Structural containment only: a body may carry more than is pinned, never less.
how_to_read.negated: false (the default) requires a matching node that is NOT beneath a `not`; true requires one that IS. Without this, wrapping a pinned conjunct in `not` would satisfy a containment check while inverting the requirement.
how_to_read.disjoined: false (the default) requires a matching node that is NOT beneath an `any`: the body must DEMAND the conjunct, not merely mention it in one branch of a disjunction. true permits a match inside one, for a requirement that is genuinely conditional, and then `disjoined_why` must name the condition. RC2-02 is why it exists and it was measured, not argued: disjoining each of the three pinned conjuncts of criterion.SalesAgreement.performed.v1 with `present(/payload/agreed_terms)` -- a field records.schema.json already requires of every SalesAgreement -- left every pin matching, this file untouched, and validate_contracts.py at exit 0 with 31 of 31 negative fixtures still rejecting, over a criterion that demanded none of it. Four rows opt in; each names its branch. Disjunction is read through negation rather than beside it, because `not(any(A, B))` demands `not A` while `not(all(A, B))` demands neither.
how_to_read.disjoined_why: required on a row with `disjoined: true` and REFUSED on any other row. An opt-out of the demand rule states which condition makes the requirement conditional, in the same way `unpinnable` states why no conjunct can carry a finding: an excuse nobody had to write is an excuse nobody reads.
how_to_read.states_exactly: the binding's `states` list must equal this set. A superset is a weakening -- `['delivered','proposed']` admits the exact counterexample AD-013 was decided to refuse -- and a subset is a different requirement than the one recorded.
how_to_read.closed_key_set: validate_contracts.py declares the constraint keys it reads and REFUSES any other key in a row. A pin whose constraint the checker silently ignored would be the same defect one layer up: a control that reads as enforcement while nothing checks it.

admissible_ancestors_why: RC4-02, and it is the structural rule this whole block now turns on: A REGISTRY MAY CLASSIFY POSITIONS; ONLY THIS FILE MAY SAY WHAT SATISFIES ONE. RC3-01's repair moved the definition of "demanded" out of a hard-coded triple in validate_contracts.py and into primitive-registry.json's `argument_positions` -- which the derivation's author also writes. The fourth recheck measured what that bought: register a NEW primitive `every_linked_obligation` with `argument_types.predicate: "boolean"` and `argument_positions.predicate: "demanded"`, wrap the three pinned conjuncts of criterion.SalesAgreement.performed.v1 in it, regenerate -- and the tree passes at exit 0 with 288,665 checks and 36 of 36 negative fixtures still rejecting, over a registry in which those conjuncts sit inside a quantifier over `/payload/obligation_refs`, a field records.schema.json gives no `minItems`. G2-01's counterexample, restored by a primitive that declared itself demanding. The table was closed against the UNDECLARED and open to the MISDECLARED. This table closes the second half: a pinned conjunct counts as demanded only when EVERY operator it sits inside, through a slot the registry calls a predicate position, is named here -- whatever `argument_positions` says about that operator. A primitive that declares its own child demanded and is not named here refuses the match, and the message names the operator.

all.why: The conjunction. A child of `all` is true exactly when the body is, so a pinned conjunct sitting inside one is demanded with no condition. Measured over the committed corpus: every chain of demand-bearing ancestors of a matched pin row is drawn from `all`, `not` and `any` and from nothing else -- 3,318 of the RC-03 walk's positions sit under `('all',)` alone -- so this table costs no live match today and refuses every operator a future author could add.

not.why: Negation is admissible because its whole effect on demand is POLARITY, and the row already states its polarity: `negated: true` requires a match beneath an odd number of `not`s and the default requires one beneath an even number. The containment filter in validate_contracts.py compares the two before this rule runs, so this entry is a backstop over that filter rather than the live control -- stated plainly, because a declaration whose condition nothing evaluates is the RC4 class one layer up. For a pinned VALUE op polarity is not a question at all (`path` and `resolve` return a JsonValue), and one live row matches a `path` reached through `eq.left` beneath `('all','any','not')`; `row_polarity` admits it for that reason and not by accident.

any.why: RC2-02's operator, and the only CONDITIONAL entry here. A conjunct kept verbatim in one branch of an `any` is contained by the body and demanded by nothing, so an `any` ancestor is admissible only for a row that opted in with `disjoined: true` and named its branch in `disjoined_why`. Four rows do, and the ceiling of four in validate_contracts.py is what stops a fifth arriving quietly. Read `admits` honestly: this condition and `not`'s are BACKSTOPS. The ancestor rule runs over the entries that would already satisfy the row, which the disjunction and polarity filters shaped first, so neither condition can fail on a tree those filters passed. MEMBERSHIP in this table is the live control; the conditions are written and evaluated so that the table states its reasons in something a checker reads rather than in prose.

admissible_ancestors_not_admitted.forall: The registry's fourth boolean-child primitive, and RC3-01's route. `quantified` is unconditionally non-demanding here: a `forall` over a collection nothing forces non-empty is vacuously true, and nothing in this corpus forces any collection non-empty. Deliberately NOT given a conditional entry -- see RC4-04 and the note the quantifier refusal prints. Demanding the collection non-empty on a sibling conjunct does NOT lift the rule.
admissible_ancestors_not_admitted.anything else: Any primitive not named in `admissible_ancestors` -- including one registered tomorrow that declares its own `boolean` child `demanded`. That is RC4-02, and it is the reason this table is a closed set of NAMES rather than a rule over roles.

argument_positions_digest_why: RC4-01. `primitive-registry.json` is written by tools/author_phase_content.py, tools/repair_r2_bootstrap_root.py and tools/repair_r3_intrinsic_subjects.py, and before this line nothing asserted a byte of it: the criterion-content drift oracle never compares the file, the guard ratchet only budgets sibling collisions, and there was no hash anywhere in the package. The fourth recheck flipped ONE string -- `/forall/argument_positions/predicate` from `"quantified"` to `"demanded"` -- and the vacuous-`forall` body validated at 288,646 checks with every pin satisfied, the census still reporting `under_quantifier: 0` because the census reads the same table. The only thing that refused it was a negative fixture naming `forall` by hand, and the sentence it printed named the FIXTURE rather than the table. This digest is sha256 over `{name: argument_positions}` for every primitive, sorted keys, compact separators, and it is MAINTAINED BY HAND: any edit to any argument position of any primitive fails the build until someone writes the new digest here, which is a line in a diff a reviewer sees. Recompute it with: python3 -c "import json,hashlib; p=json.load(open('primitive-registry.json')); print(hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({k:v['argument_positions'] for k,v in sorted(p.items())},sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':')).encode()).hexdigest())"

pinned_transitions_why:
A conjunct pin holds a guard to what it must DEMAND. It says nothing about whether the edge exists at all, and RC-01 was exactly that shape of defect: every guard was well formed, every criterion was sourced, and a delivery that failed in flight had nowhere to go. Deleting a transition is a one-line edit to record-registry.json that no check in this package noticed -- phase reachability is not checked, and a phase with fewer ways in is not a phase with fewer conjuncts. These rows are hand-written for the same reason the conjunct pins are: nothing derives them, so regenerating cannot satisfy them.

F6D-04 extends this table from 6 rows to 32. The six it had were all on `Fulfillment` and `SalesAgreement`, and NOT ONE of the fifteen WORK-1.1 records had a pinned transition -- so the earlier repair pinned the instances it found and the new layer arrived with none. Measured: three edge deletions, `ConsequenceDerivation: recomputed_at_release -> parked_on_mismatch`, `AcceptanceInterval: in_acceptance -> rejected` and `StandingHolder: staffed -> suspended`, three validator runs, three exit 0. Every edge named in `pinned_attachments` is pinned here as well, because the two attacks are different: deleting the CALL leaves the route and removes the check, deleting the TRANSITION leaves the check and removes the route, and each control is blind to the other's attack.

pinned_transitions.why: A delivery that fails IN FLIGHT. Without this edge `delivering` exits only to `delivered` or `superseded`, so the only route to `failed` runs through a delivery that was correlated -- which is the contradiction RC-01 names.
Refunding an undelivered sale -- the commonest refund there is -- was unrepresentable while `refunded` had one inbound edge, from `delivered`.
The other half of the same requirement: `refunded` is reachable from BOTH, and a repair that added one route by deleting the other would satisfy a looser reading of the finding.
RC-08: without it the generic validation branch and the delivery branch are disjoint, so a validated Fulfillment can only be delivered by a route that skipped validation.
The edge AD-013's delivery evidence hangs on. Its conjuncts are pinned above; this pins that there is an edge for them to be conjuncts OF.
The route OUT of residuals. Without it `terminated_with_residuals` is a terminal state that keeps its duties forever, which is a different contract from the one AD-014 decided.

(PROSE_PATH). English nouns are not compared to conjuncts, and most of what these sentences are made of is English nouns.
